about: Religious structures — temples, mazars and dargahs, mosques, madrasas, gurdwaras, churches — demolished or removed in India as encroachments, 2014–2026, as counted by governments, courts and reporting. 'Illegal' is the authorities' designation; many were contested in court.

records.window: Drive from April 2023 to early May 2023, forest land
records.who: Chief Conservator of Forests, as reported
records.quote: The drive has demolished 200 tombs and 27 temples in the state.
At least 280 religious structures which were illegally built on government land have been demolished which include 260 Mazars and 20 temples.

records.who: An unnamed government official, quoted by ThePrint and re-reported
records.quote: About 465 mazars (mausoleums), 45 temples, and two encroachments by the gurudwara committee had been demolished.
records.notes: The gurdwara entries are 'encroachments by the gurudwara committee', not necessarily whole gurdwaras. ThePrint's original was not reachable; the figure is attested by two secondary reports.

records.who: District officials, as reported by a pro-government outlet
records.quote: Nearly 600 illegal structures have already been cleared across the state as part of the ongoing campaign.
records.notes: No breakdown by faith. Another compilation cites 538 removed structures from official reports. In April 2023 the Chief Minister said over a thousand such structures had been identified — a count of sites found, not demolished.

records.who: State government, in a reply to the Legislative Assembly, as reported
records.quote: The state government informed the State Legislative Assembly that 108 mazars had been demolished during anti-encroachment operations.
records.notes: An assembly reply as reported by two advocacy outlets; the reply itself was not found. Only mazars are counted in it as reported; other faiths' structures in the same period are not stated.

records.who: State government, to the Gujarat High Court (suo motu PIL)
records.quote: 604 unauthorized religious structures have been removed from public land/ streets/ spaces in the last two months.
records.notes: 318 in district areas and 286 in municipal corporations. A further 87 were relocated and 6 regularised. No breakdown by faith.

records.quote: Nine religious sites and 45 residential buildings were demolished as part of the anti-encroachment drive.
records.notes: Reports describe the nine as mosques, dargahs and shrines; a graveyard was also cleared. May overlap with the High Court figure's period.

records.who: State government, to the Gujarat High Court
records.quote: 48 religious encroachments were removed, 38 relocated and more than 30 regularised in the state in last two months.
records.notes: 468 notices issued, per the same hearing; in February 2025 the state reported 458.

records.window: Drive along the Nepal border, May 2025
records.quote: More than 350 unauthorised religious sites, including madrasas, mosques, mazars and Eidgahs, were sealed or demolished.
records.notes: 350+ is sealed or demolished; 286 is the demolished count with a breakdown, from a pro-government outlet at a later point in the same drive.

records.who: Delhi Development Authority, to the Delhi High Court
records.quote: The DDA said it had identified and demolished 127 illegal religious structures.
records.notes: 82 of the 127 were identified by the forest department. Delhi's religious committee had recommended 249 matters for removal.

records.quote: The state was able to demolish, relocate and regulate only 2,887 of them.
records.notes: Starts before 2014 and includes relocated and regularised structures, so it is not a demolition count for this page's period. The state still counted 6,395 unauthorised religious structures in public places in 2021; after a temple demolition at Nanjangud that September, the government halted the drive and passed a law to protect existing structures.

cases.what: Guru Ravidas temple at Tughlakabad, in a protected forest, demolished by the DDA after a Supreme Court order of April 2019.
Little Flower Church, Lado Sarai, demolished as encroachment on government agricultural land; the diocese cited a stay from 2015.
Temple at Nanjangud, Mysuru, demolished under the Supreme Court's 2009 order; the state halted the drive after protests.
Temples at Rajgarh, Alwar, demolished in a road-widening anti-encroachment drive.
Sher Ali Baba mazar in Corbett Tiger Reserve demolished by the forest department; caretakers say they were not heard.
Masjid Akhonji and a madrasa at Mehrauli demolished by the DDA on the religious committee's recommendation.
Mosques, dargahs and a graveyard near Somnath demolished; 135 people detained.
Dhubri eviction: about 1,700 structures, homes and mosques among them, demolished; residents say temples nearby were left standing.

compilations.name: Millat Times compilation
compilations.what: Reported instances, structures or aggregate figures of demolition, removal or eviction affecting Muslim religious and community properties.
compilations.caveat: Mixes single cases with government totals, partial demolitions and overlapping aggregates; counts Muslim sites only. Dawn cites 2,126 from the same work.

law.what: The Supreme Court bars new unauthorised religious structures on public streets, parks and places, and orders states to review existing ones case by case — remove, relocate or regularise. It applies to every faith.
The Supreme Court requires 15 days' notice, a hearing and video for demolitions — but excludes unauthorised structures on roads, footpaths, railway land and water bodies.

views.said: The drives reclaim government, forest and border land and clear roads under court orders, and are not aimed at any community.
Muslim shrines are removed far more often than temples on the same land; some sites were waqf property or centuries old, and owners were not heard.
